Documentation → Administration → Settings → Scout (AI)

Scout settings (AI assistant)

Turn Scout, the AI assistant (formerly AI Advisor), on, decide whether it may call read-only tools and external providers, and manage the provider registry (Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic) with a test call before saving.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsadvisor.configure
📍 WhereSettings → System → Scout (URL /settings/#tab-ai)

What is it?#

The Scout tab configures the Scout AI chat: three feature switches and the list of model providers it may use. The assistant never writes to SATOM or an appliance directly. Local Ollama traffic stays on your network; anything sent to an external provider — the new message and the earlier conversation turns sent with it — is redacted of known internal identifiers first and recorded in the Audit log as advisor.send. An Ollama provider counts as local only when its Base URL host is localhost, a loopback, link-local or private address; an Ollama provider on a public or unresolvable host is treated as external.

ℹ️Note

Renamed on 2026-10-14: this tab was called AI Advisor until then. The settings group that used to be called Scout, for the fault-localisation ladder, is now Path Diagnostics (see Path Diagnostics settings). The anchor #tab-ai and the ai.* setting names are unchanged.

What does it do?#

  • Enable Scout — feature master switch (default off).
  • Allow read-only tool calls (mode C) — lets the model call read-only tools (default off).
  • Allow external providers — a second gate, required in addition to a configured external provider (default off).
  • Providers — add, edit, delete, test and choose the default provider.

Each switch saves immediately when toggled.

Requirements#

  • advisor.configure and administrator rights (users.manage): the entry sits in the admin-only System group and is additionally hidden from administrators without advisor.configure.
  • A reachable model: a local Ollama host, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or the Anthropic API.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

All /settings/ai/* routes require advisor.configure; without it they return 403 and the menu entry is not shown. Chatting with Scout needs advisor.use (see Scout).

How to use#

Turn Scout on#

  1. Open Settings → System → Scout.
  2. Switch on Enable Scout. Leave the other two switches off to keep everything on your network.

Add a provider#

  1. Click Add provider.
  2. Fill Key (slug, unique), Label, Kind, Base URL, Model and, for external providers, API key.
  3. Click Test connection. One trivial chat call is made with the form's current values (not yet saved): "OK — <the model's reply>" or "Failed — <error>". When editing with a blank API key, the stored key is used.
  4. Click Save. The provider appears in the list; the first provider, or the one you mark with Make default, carries the default badge.

Edit or delete#

  • Edit opens the form; the key cannot be changed; a blank API key keeps the stored one.
  • Delete asks Delete provider "<key>"? and also removes its stored API key.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Key (slug, unique) Identifier; saving an existing key replaces that provider. Yes openai-corp
Label Display name; blank = the key. No Corporate gateway
Kind Ollama (local, no API key), OpenAI-compatible (ChatGPT / Azure OpenAI / LiteLLM / vLLM…), Anthropic (Claude Messages API). Yes OpenAI-compatible
Base URL Endpoint; a trailing / is removed. For an Ollama provider, the host decides whether it counts as local (loopback, link-local, private address or localhost) or external (any other host). Yes https://llm.example.com/v1
Model Model name as the provider expects it. Yes gpt-4o-mini
API key Encrypted at rest, never shown again; blank keeps the stored key (or none for Ollama). External —

ℹ️Note — Placeholders and the automatic local provider

The Base URL placeholder shows generic examples (http://localhost:11434 or https://api.openai.com/v1); enter your own host. When the list is empty, opening the Scout chat page (not this tab) creates a provider ollama-local (Local Ollama, http://localhost:11434, model qwen2.5-coder:32b) disabled, and makes it the default — edit its Base URL to your own Ollama host, enable it and save.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: an Ollama provider whose Base URL host is public or cannot be resolved is treated as external — its traffic is redacted, needs Allow external providers and is recorded as an export; and the shipped placeholders and the seeded ollama-local provider no longer point at a deployment-specific address.

Example#

🧪Example — Local first, external on request

Add ollama-lab (Ollama, http://{ip}:11434 — a private address, so it counts as local; model qwen2.5-coder:32b), test, save, Make default. Add claude (Anthropic) with an API key but leave Allow external providers off; users can only chat locally until you switch that gate on.

Result#

  • Flags and providers are stored in app_settings (ai.enabled, ai.tools_enabled, ai.external_allowed, ai.default_provider, ai.providers); each API key is stored encrypted under its own key.
  • Changes apply to the next chat message.

Troubleshooting#

"a provider key is required"#

Solution — fill Key (slug, unique) before saving.

"unknown provider kind '…'"#

Solution — choose one of the three kinds in the list.

Test shows "Failed — …"#

Possible causes — wrong Base URL or model name, missing or invalid API key, or the host is unreachable from the SATOM node. A large local model can take a long time to load on a cold call.

Solution — correct the values and test again; for Ollama, check the model is pulled on the host.

Users get "external providers are disabled -- turn on \"Allow external providers\" …"#

Possible causes — the default (or chosen) provider is external and Allow external providers is off.

Solution — switch the gate on, or make a local provider the default.

An Ollama provider is treated as external#

Possible causes — its Base URL host is a public address, a public DNS name, or a name the SATOM node cannot resolve. Only localhost and loopback, link-local or private addresses count as local.

Solution — point Base URL at the Ollama host's private address (or a name that resolves to one), or keep it external and switch Allow external providers on.

Verification — chatting with that provider no longer reports that external providers are disabled while the gate is off.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • The test call is never stored or exported; it uses a 20-second timeout.
  • Deleting the default provider makes the first remaining provider the default.
  • This tab loads its own state from /settings/ai/state, so it works independently of the rest of the Settings page.
